messages:
Diego: heads-up — saw a 3x tail-latency spike in eu-central around 20:03 UTC when a tenant ramped. Dedicated slices seemed to hit 90%+ GPU util, requests queued, some routed to cold fallback and timed out. Anyone tracking a similar pattern?

ops-bot: ALERT: eu-central rack-7 GPU util 92% (5m avg) · incident-id: igpu-2026-03-20-euc7

Maria: yikes. saw the alert too. could be KV cache thrash + egress bottleneck. quick triage: check kvcache hit rate + egress queues on those slices. if warm pool consumption is high, trigger spillover routing to reserved hot-lane or dedicated fallback.

Liam: cost note — spilling > dedicated fallback will blow out cost if we route NTP traffic to dedicated. prefer throttling or short-lived preemptible carveouts first.

Diego: agreed on cost. also noticed NIC queue drops on node-42 in the logs; might be interrupt/irq coalescing causing uneven ingress. attaching a small excerpt: 

```
Mar 20 20:03:04 node-42 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: NIC tx_queue 2 dropped pkts=1240
Mar 20 20:03:05 proxy: route-decider: spillover triggered for slice s-euc-42 (egress_q_len=1200)
Mar 20 20:03:07 runtime: kvcache miss rate 0.76 (baseline 0.12)
```

Maria: for immediate mitigation I recommend this quick checklist: 
1) enable soft-ratecap on non-SLA tenants (route tag: non-sla -> rate=0.6)
2) increase warm-pool size for eu-central by +10% (temporary)
3) flip spillover policy to prefer local dedicated pools with prewarmed instances (policy id: spill-prewarm-v3)
4) monitor egress backlog and kvcache hit for 15m, revert if cost > threshold

Sarah: who owns the runbook for surge protection? we should make these steps playbookified.

Maria: I can own the runbook. quick commands to flip policies: 

```
# prefer dedicated fallback for eu-central
redwoodctl routing update --region eu-central --policy spillover=spill-prewarm-v3
# soft-cap non-sla tenants
redwoodctl tenant update --selector tier=non-sla --set rate_limit=0.6
# bump warm pool
redwoodctl pool adjust --region eu-central --pool warm-pool --delta +10%
```

Liam: can we add a short-circuit check to auto-scale warm-pool when kvcache miss rate > 0.5 for 3m? otherwise manual flips will lag the surge.

Maria: good idea. I'll sketch an autoscale rule: kvcache_miss_ratio > 0.5 for 180s -> warm-pool +15% (cooldown 10m). also set a cost cap to prevent runaway.

Diego: +1. also add an egress-headroom gauge so routing prefers nodes with free NIC queue capacity. that should reduce cross-node tail latency.

Sarah: next steps: Maria to PR runbook w/ commands + rollback steps; Diego to add egress-headroom gauge as a signal; Liam to draft cost-safeguards for autoscale. I'll coordinate review. :thumbsup:

Maria: will PR today, tag @sarah and @liam. starting with conservative defaults.

Diego: thanks — ping here once PR is up and I'll run the mitigation on the canary rack first.

ops-bot: NOTE: mitigation started on canary rack-3 at 20:12 UTC (spill-prewarm-v3 applied)

Liam: monitoring dash looks healthier already — tail p95 dropping back toward normal.

Sarah: great job team. let's formalize this into the infra runbook and include the CLI snippets.
